title: Belief-Calibrated Optimization: An Explicit World Model for Agentic Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2609.01861v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The performance of an LLM agent depends on the scaffold around a frozen model. A common way to improve that scaffold is to use a coding agent as an optimizer: it reads current scores and traces and iteratively edits the source, producing a new candidate each round. Each edit is chosen according to a belief about how the environment will respond: what went wrong, and which change should help. That belief is typically implicit. It lives in the coding agent's reasoning on the current call, or remains latent in its parameters, rather than as something written down. Later calls therefore see scores and traces, but they do not use that belief. We introduce Belief-Calibrated Optimization (BCO), a method that writes that belief down as a persistent in-context document and continually revises that document as new candidates are evaluated. The resulting document is a world model: the current account of how the environment responds to edits. Added

translated_title: 信念校准优化：面向智能体优化的显式世界模型
translated_abstract: LLM智能体的性能取决于围绕冻结模型的脚手架。改进该脚手架的一种常见方法是使用编码智能体作为优化器：它读取当前的分数和执行轨迹，并迭代地编辑源代码，每一轮产生一个新的候选方案。每次编辑都是根据一种关于环境将如何响应的信念来选择的：哪里出了问题，以及哪种修改应该会有所帮助。这种信念通常是隐式的，它存在于编码智能体在当前调用中的推理过程里，或者潜藏在其参数中，而不是以书面形式记录下来。因此，后续的调用虽然能看到分数和轨迹，但并不会利用这种信念。我们提出了信念校准优化，这是一种将该信念显式记录为一份持久的上下文内文档、并随着新候选方案的评估而持续修订该文档的方法。最终得到的文档就是一个世界模型：关于环境如何响应编辑操作的当前描述。
tldr: 该论文提出信念校准优化（BCO），将优化器中隐式的环境响应信念显式化为一份持久存在、随新候选方案评估而不断修订的上下文内文档（即世界模型），从而让后续的智能体优化过程能够利用这一显式信念来指导代码改进。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes Belief-Calibrated Optimization (BCO), which externalizes the optimizer's implicit beliefs about environment responses into a persistent, continually revised in-context document (a world model), enabling subsequent agentic optimization steps to leverage this explicit belief when improving code.
